previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and an implanted defibrillator was admitted for dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea after a recent similar hospitalization. He presented with fluid overload, confirmed by weight gain, elevated BNP, and radiographic evidence of interstitial pulmonary edema. His symptoms improved with oral furosemide, and his weight returned to baseline. Cardiac enzymes were negative, and EKGs unchanged, ruling out acute coronary syndrome; chest pressure was attributed to musculoskeletal pain. Lisinopril was restarted at a low dose with plans for outpatient kidney function monitoring. An albuterol inhaler was prescribed for respiratory symptoms. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions on daily weight monitoring, medication adherence, and follow-up care.
